gloss: to be frozen with fear; to have one's legs go weak

definitions.gloss: to be frozen with fear; to have one's legs go weak
definitions.explanation: To become unable to move one's legs due to fear, anxiety, or shock. Describes the physical sensation of legs becoming stiff or weak from fright.

examples.japanese: {高|たか}いところで{足|あし}がすくむ。
examples.english: My legs freeze up at high places.

examples.japanese: {崖|がけ}の{上|うえ}に{立|た}つと{足|あし}がすくんだ。
examples.english: My legs went weak when I stood at the top of the cliff.

examples.japanese: {暗|くら}い{路地|ろじ}で{物音|ものおと}がして、{足|あし}がすくんで{動|うご}けなくなった。
examples.english: I heard a noise in the dark alley and my legs froze, unable to move.

notes:
すくむ means to cower, stiffen, or become paralyzed with fear. This expression vividly describes the physical sensation of legs becoming stiff or weak from fright.

COMMON TRIGGERS:
- {高|たか}いところ: high places
- {暗|くら}い{場所|ばしょ}: dark places
- {突然|とつぜん}の{恐怖|きょうふ}: sudden fright
- {危険|きけん}な{状況|じょうきょう}: dangerous situations

RELATED EXPRESSIONS:
- {立|た}ちすくむ: to stand frozen in place (unable to move at all)
- {身|み}がすくむ: to freeze up (whole body, not just legs)
- {腰|こし}が{抜|ぬ}ける: to go weak in the knees (stronger — completely unable to stand)
- {足|あし}が{震|ふる}える: legs tremble (shaking rather than freezing)

GRAMMAR:
The subject is {足|あし} (legs), not the person. The person experiencing fear is marked with の or は: {私|わたし}は{足|あし}がすくんだ.
